periodos.nombre: Late Bronze — Canaanite city on the coastal plain
Iron I — Philistine city, recipient of the ark
Iron II — Philistine city, center of worship of Baal-Zebub

descripcion_geo: Ekron (Hebrew: עֶקְרוֹן; Philistine: Amqaruna) was the northernmost of the five cities of the Philistine Pentapolis, located at the northern end of the Philistine plain, in the transition zone with the Shephelah of Judah. Definitively identified with Tel Miqne (excavated 1981-1996), it is one of the best documented Iron I-II archaeological sites in the Levant. The 20-hectare tell revealed a city with more than one hundred olive oil production facilities in the Iron IIC period (7th century BC), the largest known olive industry in the ancient world. A royal dedicatory inscription in the Philistine language mentions King Ikausu (Achish) of Amqaruna, confirming the identification of the place.
clima: Plain coastal Mediterranean — rainfall of 450-500 mm annually, warm summers moderated by sea breezes, mild winters. Fertile alluvial soils suitable for intensive olive groves.
recursos: Olive oil industry — more than one hundred presses from the 7th century BC. (archaeologically confirmed)
Plain agriculture (wheat, barley, grapevine, olive tree)
Trade with Assyria, Egypt and the Eastern Mediterranean
Route control between the Philistine plain and the Judah highlands
importancia_estrategica: Ekron was the closest Philistine city to the Israelite territory of Judah and Dan, which made it a constant point of friction. Its olive oil industry from the 7th century operated under an Assyrian protectorate, evidencing the economic integration of the city-state into the imperial system. The god Baal-Zebub of Ekron, consulted by King Ahaziah of Israel, became the symbol par excellence of the foreign cult that threatened Yahwist fidelity.

otros_habitantes.descripcion: The royal inscription of Ekron (7th century BC) is one of the only known Philistine language texts and mentions five consecutive kings of the city. The Philistines of Ekron developed a sophisticated olive-growing industry under the Assyria protectorate after Sennacherib's campaign (701 BC), becoming suppliers of oil to the empire. This pragmatic adaptation to Assyrian power contrasts with the resistance of other Philistine cities.
otros_habitantes.religion: Philistine polytheism — main cult of Baal-Zebub (lord of the flies or lord from above), with assimilation of Canaanites cults

otros_habitantes.nombre: Israelites from the tribe of Dan
otros_habitantes.descripcion: The territory originally assigned to Dan included cities near Ekron (Josh 19:43). Philistine pressure prevented Dan from taking effective possession of their inheritance on the plain, finally forcing the Danite migration north (Judges 18). The area between Ekron and the hills of Judah was territory of permanent conflict, where figures like Samson operated on the cultural border between Israelites and Philistines.
otros_habitantes.religion: Yahwism tribal with syncretism — the tribe of Dan later established an idol shrine in their new northern location (Judg 18:30-31)

historias.titulo: The ark reaches Ekron: the plague they could not stop
historias.descripcion: When the ark wreaked havoc on Ashdod and then Gath, the Philistines lords sent it to Ekron. The Ekronites, seeing it arriving, cried out: 'They have brought the ark of the God of Israel to us to kill us all!' The entire city was struck with a deadly plague. The voices of those who were dying reached heaven. Messrs. Philistines called an emergency meeting. His priests and soothsayers recommended the return of the ark with an atoning offering of golden tumors and golden mice—one for each Philistine city—implicitly recognizing the power of Yahweh. Ekron was the ark's last station in Philistine territory, the point where the coalition of the five cities decided that no price was too high to return that devastating object.

historias.titulo: Ahaziah consults Baal-Zebub: the king who asked the wrong god
historias.descripcion: King Ahaziah of Israel fell through the latticework of his room in Samaria and was seriously injured. Instead of consulting the prophet of Yahweh, he sent messengers to consult Baal-Zebub, god of Ekron, to see if he would recover. The prophet Elijah intercepted them on the way with a withering message: 'Is there no God in Israel that you should go and consult Baal-Zebub, god of Ekron? Therefore you will not come down from the bed where you have climbed, but you will die.' The king sent a captain with fifty men to bring Elijah. The prophet called down fire from heaven and consumed them. A second group suffered the same fate. The third captain prostrated himself before Elijah begging for his life. The prophet came down and repeated the same oracle of death before the king. Ahaziah died without a son, and his brother Joram reigned in his place.

historias.titulo: Ekron under Assyria: the oil industrial city
historias.descripcion: After Sennacherib's campaign (701 BC), Ekron was transformed into an industrial center under Assyrian protectorate. Archeology has revealed that in the 7th century the city reached its maximum extent (20 hectares) and developed an unprecedented olive oil industry: more than one hundred pressing facilities, capable of producing hundreds of tons of oil per year for export to the Assyrian and Mediterranean markets. A royal Philistine inscription of King Ikausu dedicates a temple to his goddess. This period of material prosperity coincided with the prophetic denunciation of Zephaniah and Amos against the Philistine cities. Ekron was finally destroyed by Nebuchadnezzar in 604 BC, confirmed by both the biblical text (Jer 25:20) and the Babylonian chronicles.

personajes.rol: Prophet of fire, defender of Yahwist exclusivity
personajes.descripcion: The Elijah of the Ekron episode is the same prophet of Carmel, but in a different context: he does not summon the people to choose between Yahweh and Baal, but rather he intercepts the consultation of a dying king to the foreign god. His rhetorical question—'Is there no God in Israel?'—is the theological core of the episode: the consultation of Baal-Zebub is not only religious infidelity but an implicit declaration that Yahweh is incapable of or does not deserve to be consulted. The fire that consumes the captains is reminiscent of the fire of Carmel: Elijah is the prophet whose word has physical power over nature.

personajes.rol: King of Israel, son of Ahab, killed for consulting Baal-Zebub
personajes.descripcion: Ahaziah ben Ahab reigned over Israel for only two years. The son of King Ahab and Queen Jezebel, he continued the religious policy of his parents—the cult of Baal that had characterized their dynasty. His decision to consult Baal-Zebub of Ekron in the face of an illness is read by the biblical text as the act that sealed his fate: not only was it idolatrous but it revealed a radical distrust in Yahweh. He died without an heir, closing his dynastic line, and was succeeded by his brother Joram. The text mentions him briefly, as a negative echo of his father Ahab.

The 'seren' (lords) Philistines are the governing council of the five cities of the Pentapolis: Gaza, Ashkelon, Ashdod, Ekron and Gath. They always appear acting in council, reflecting an unusual confederal political structure in the Late Bronze-Iron I Levant. In the ark episodes, they displayed pragmatic rationality: they consulted their own priests and diviners, recognized the power of Yahweh without converting to it, and adopted the least costly solution (returning the ark with offerings). In the episode of Samson (Judge 16), they called the great assembly in the temple of Dagon of Gaza that ended in the death of the judge and three thousand Philistines.

contexto_religioso.contexto_lugar: Ekron is the Philistine city that appears at both ends of the theological spectrum of the OT: first as a victim of the power of Yahweh (Ark episode), then as the center of the cult of Baal-Zebub that attracts the consultation of the king of Israel. The name 'Baal-Zebub' (בַּעַל זְבוּב, 'lord of the flies') may be a mocking deformation of the original name 'Baal-Zebul' ('lord of the palace/exalted'), transformed by the biblical redactors into an insult. This same deformation survived in the NT as the name of the prince of demons ('Beelzebub').
religiones_presentes: Philistine polytheism — worship of Baal-Zebub as main oracular deity
Israelite Yahwism — presence of the ark as a sign of Yahweh sovereignty

mitos.nombre: Baal-Zebub of Ekron: from the Philistine god to the prince of demons

judaismo.fuente_secundaria: Talmud Bavli, Sanedrín 102b; Targum Jonatán sobre 2 Re 1:2
judaismo.descripcion: The Targum Jonathan (Aramaic translation of the OT) paraphrases Ahaziah's consultation of Baal-Zebub as 'consulting the fly idol of Ekron', underlining the degrading aspect of the name. Rabbinic tradition (Sanhedrin 102b) used the episode of Ahaziah as an extreme example of royal apostasy: a king of Israel who, having access to prophets of Yahweh, preferred to consult a foreign god. The episode was read as proof that Ahab's house was hopelessly corrupt.
judaismo.similitudes: All three traditions associate Baal-Zebub with forces opposed to God.
judaismo.diferencias: Judaism treats Baal-Zebub as an idol with no real power; the NT elevates him to the rank of demonic prince.
judaismo.significado_teologico: Consulting other gods is an implicit declaration that Yahweh cannot or will not respond—practical rather than theological apostasy.
judaismo.posible_relacion_cultural: The name Baal-Zebul ('exalted lord') appears in Ugaritic texts as an epithet for Baal, confirming that the biblical form 'Zebub' (flies) is an intentional degrading alteration.

cristianismo.fuente_secundaria: Orígenes, Contra Celso VII,17; Jerónimo, Comentario sobre Mateo 12:24
cristianismo.descripcion: In the gospels, the Pharisees accuse Jesus of casting out demons 'by Beelzebul, the prince of demons' (Mt 12:24). The Philistine name of Ekron has been transformed into the title of God's supreme adversary. Jesus responds with the logical argument: a kingdom divided against itself cannot stand — if I cast out demons by Beelzebul, by whom do your children cast them out? The use of the name connects the Christological controversy of the NT with the ancient anti-idolatrous controversy of the OT: the god of Ekron who seduced Ahaziah becomes the adversary that religious leaders attribute to Jesus.
cristianismo.similitudes: Baal-Zebub's association with demonic evil is a direct continuity between AT and NT.
cristianismo.diferencias: The OT treats it as an inert idol; the NT personifies him as a spiritual being with real power but subordinate to Christ.
cristianismo.significado_teologico: The accusation of acting by Beelzebul is the blasphemy that Jesus refutes with his most logical argument from the gospels: good cannot come from evil.
